subject: breaking up a gene into exon counts

messages.author: 0726a6b219eeafcd
messages.subject: breaking up a gene into exon counts
parts:
Hi all, perhaps I mistaken, but I was under the impression that subread can count by exons? Such that if a gene has 10 exons, then the return data would be something like, 

genex-exon1 - count
genex-exon2 - count etc.. 

What I'm interested is to compare say, exon1 to exon2 and so fourth.  For example a bar graph showing the different fragment count by exon, perhaps even normalized to the length of the exon. 

the command I'm using is,
 featureCounts -F SAF -p -s 2 -g gene_id -t exon -a /s/subread/annotation/hg19_RefSeq_exon.txt -o ... and so on

is it possible to instead of returning fragment counts by gene to have it return exon by exon?

thank you! 

Alex

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: breaking up a gene into exon counts
parts:
Adding '-f' to your command will get you exon counts.

Wei

messages.author: 0726a6b219eeafcd
messages.subject: Re: breaking up a gene into exon counts
parts:
perfect! thanks.  works exactly how I wanted.  Should I expect all the counts from the different exons to sum up exactly? 
Alex

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: breaking up a gene into exon counts
parts:
If you just want to get counts for exons, then the '-f' option has done the job. So why do you want to sum up counts across exons? Do you actually want to get counts for genes?

Wei
